column1: # Key of the code of Resident Johan von Lilienthal, Moscow 1665-1667 (lead 2316; Riksarkivet, Diplomatica Muscovitica
# SE/RA/2113/2113.1/1/36/82, series R0000814), rebuilt by Brice Dudout (Claude Opus 5.5 agents), 10 Nov 2026.
# Licence: CC BY 4.0, Brice Dudout (the key table as rebuilt here; the glosses it comes from are the decipherment of the time).
# German letter substitution with homophones (also ch, sch, st, ss, ll, ff, tz; u = v = w), 2-3 digit groups separated by dots,
# mixed with clear German. Six code series: 23-59, 63-100, 103-150, 153-190, 293-349, 353-390 (numbers ending in 1 or 2 do
# not occur). Series 293-349 repeats the letter order of 23-59 (+270, then +290), series 353-390 that of 63-100 (+290).
# Learned from the contemporary glosses of images 42 (both pages) and 47 (left) only (97 glossed runs, 1116 aligned groups,
# no conflict; frozen/PAIRES-LILIENTHAL.tsv), frozen (SHA-256 81f56ea7...dbca), then measured once on image 45 (validation.txt):
# 0.887 of characters vs 0.047 for the best of 200 shuffled keys.
# "tested" = in the frozen key (column n = occurrences in the training pairs). Rows marked "post" were added AFTER the
# measurement, from the order of the table and from sense, and are outside the test.
# Status of tested rows: "sure" = seen 3 times or more in the training pairs, "probable" = once or twice.
